Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: OHIO POWER COMPANY
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 10 feet by 525 feet (area 5250 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 15 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0.13 gallons
AN AUTOMOTIVE GARAGE CAUGHT FIRE AND BURNED TO THE GROUND. A NEARBY UTILITY POLE EVENTUALLY CAUGHT FIRE, AND A POLE-MOUNT TRANSFORMER ATTACHED TO THE POLE FELL TO THE GROUND AND RELEASED APPROXIMATELY 15 GALLONS OF NO-PCB MINERAL OIL. WATER FROM THE FIRE FIGHTING EFFORTS WASHED THE RELEASED OIL TO A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. THE STORM DRAIN SYSTEM DISCHARGED TO A NEARBY CREEK LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 200 FEET TO THE NORTHWEST OF THE SITE. THERE IS ALSO A LOT OF ASH, SOOT AND OTHER UNKNOWN MATERIALS THAT HAVE ALSO WASHED INTO THE STORM DRAIN SYSTEM AND CREEK AS WELL.

THIS WAS LOCATED NEAR THE CAISSON ROAD CROSSING IN FREDERICKSBURG, VA. FOUR CARS ARE OVERTURNED; NO WATER WAYS ARE AFFECTED. STAFFORD COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE WAS NOTIFIED. UPDATE: S.R. AT 1614 HOURS, A MECHANICAL DEPARTMENT REPRESENTATIVE ADVISED TWO CARS ON THEIR SIDE, TWO WERE LEANING, AND FOUR WERE UP-RIGHT (NO CAR NUMBERS WERE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME). CRANEMASTERS WERE NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING OUT OF TINYTOWN AND HULCHER WAS NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING FROM GETTYSBURG. NO ETAS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. UPDATE: AT 1737 HOURS, A S/A ADVISED HE WAS RESPONDING AND SHOULD ARRIVE ON SCENE AT APRROXIMATELY 1900 HOURS. UPDATE: AT 1813 HOURS, AN SSA ADVISED HE WAS ON SCENE. THE ROAD WAY IS CLEAR. WAITING FOR CRANES TO ARRIVE ON SCENE. UPDATE: AT 1952 HOURS, THE MECHANICAL DESK REPORTED CARS CSXT 390190, 392297, 390746, 390714, 392105, 393721, 390680 AND 390493 WERE THE CARS THAT DERAILED. UPDATE: ON 04/27/13 AT 0044 HOURS, THE MECHANICAL DESK REPORTED ESTIMATED DAMAGE AT $86,620. UPDATE: ON 4/27/13 AT 0425 HOURS, TOTAL COST IS 175,800 DOLLARS

Report Description/// THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1417853 /// THE UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATED THAT (25) EMPLOYES WERE EVACUATED. COUNTY ROADS 550E AND 800 N WERE CLOSED IN ALL DIRECTIONS. /// ORIGINAL REPORT BELOW /// /// UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1417696 /// UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATES THAT THERE WAS A RELEASE OF ANHYDROUS AMMONIA INTO THE ATMOSPHERE FROM A CYLINOID VALVE ON THE COMPRESSOR IN THE FACILITY. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO THE CYLINOID VALVE FAILING AND BLOWING OFF THE COMPRESSOR. THE CALLER STATES THAT THE AMMONIA IGNITED DUE TO UNKNOWN REASONS AT THIS TIME, WHICH CAUSED AN EXPLOSION. THE CALLER STATES THAT THE FACILITY WAS EVACUATED OF ALL PERSONNEL, BUT THE NUMBER IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME. THE HAMILTON TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT ARRIVED ON SCENE TO SECURE THE RELEASE AND VENT THE BUILDING. THE FIRE BURNT OUT ON ITS OWN. THE CALLER STATES THAT THERE WERE NO INJURIES OR FATALITIES IN THE INCIDENT, THE CALLER ALSO STATES THAT AFTER HAMILTON FIRE DEPARTMENT AND AN UNKNOWN HAZMAT TEAM ARRIVED ON SCENE A 1.5 MILE EVACUATION RADIUS WAS IN PLACE. THE CALLER STATES THAT THERE WAS ABOUT 5 HOUSES IN THE AREA OF THE 1.5 EVACUATION RADIUS THAT WERE EVACUATED, BUT THE NUMBER OF PERSONNEL EVACUATED FROM THE HOUSES IS UNKNOWN. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS AS FOLLOWS: CALLER REPORTED A RELEASE OF AMMONIA DUE TO UNKNOWN REASONS.
